subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to follow symlinks to sibling directories inside `~/.openclaw`, and should that policy live in `@openclaw/fs-safe` or in an OpenClaw-only wrapper?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally relaxes a prompt-context filesystem boundary, and maintainer discussion already separated this security-routed issue from the broader non-security symlink PR.

options.title: Keep as security-policy tracker
options.body: Preserve this issue until maintainers choose the exact fs-safe or wrapper policy and required allow/deny tests.

options.title: Fold into the broader symlink PR
options.body: Use the open maintainer PR as canonical only if maintainers explicitly decide its narrower policy also covers `.openclaw` sibling symlinks.

options.title: Reject sibling `.openclaw` targets
options.body: Document that synced bootstrap files need copies or another supported path while keeping the workspace root as the strict runtime boundary.

recommendation.title: Keep as security-policy tracker
recommendation.body: Preserve this issue until maintainers choose the exact fs-safe or wrapper policy and required allow/deny tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the current maintainer direction and own the overlapping open bootstrap symlink PR.
